answer: Epoch-Shifted Signal Inheritance (ESSI): each agent’s trust weight is a hash of its prior-epoch interaction atlas, e.g. distinct counterparties and timing entropy. To bootstrap N sybils, an attacker must farm that exact historical pattern across ≥K epochs; each clone’s weight is capped by the minimum of its own past. Splitting into many clones lowers each one’s inherited signal, while consistent sybils require sustained cedar-costly coordination. Forgery cost scales with K × historical breadth, not just identity creation.
